messages.text: what is the amount earned per day if you mine for a pool

On a pool, the NerdQaxe++ ($249, 6 TH/s) pays small, steady sats to your own wallet every day. It uses 150 W, which is 3.6 kWh a day, or about 36¢ a day at 10¢ per kWh. What do you pay per kWh? I'll work out your exact sats per day.

At €0.20 per kWh, the NerdQaxe++ costs about €0.72 a day to run, or €21.60 a month. On a pool it would earn roughly a few hundred sats a day at today's network difficulty. The exact amount moves with the Bitcoin price and difficulty, and the pool's dashboard shows it to the sat.

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. People buy it for a shot at a full 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, around the clock, plus a real node of the network on their desk.

Is this your first miner?
Searched the catalog · Hammer Miner BC04

For a first miner, I'd get the Hammer Miner BC04 ($249) over the NerdQaxe++. Both do 6 TH/s, but the BC04 draws about 100 W instead of 150 W. At €0.20 per kWh that's about €14.40 a month instead of €21.60. It's in stock and ships within about 5 business days, while the EU-plug NerdQaxe++ is out.

It also has an ethernet port. That makes the first setup easy: plug it in, point it at a pool, add your own wallet address, and you'll watch your sats come in while you learn how mining, pools and wallets actually work.
